path_name: PL/pgSQL bound cursor variable assignment rules changed
description: PostgreSQL 16 changed how PL/pgSQL bound cursor variables are assigned their string values. Previously, the string value was set to match the variable name during cursor assignment; now it is assigned during OPEN and will not match the variable name. PL/pgSQL functions that rely on the old behavior may produce incorrect results or errors.

conditions.statement: Target PostgreSQL version is 16 or later

evidence.quote_or_summary: Change assignment rules for PL/pgSQL bound cursor variables
evidence.relevance: Documents the behavior change in PostgreSQL 16

conditions.statement: Application uses PL/pgSQL functions with bound cursor variables that depend on the cursor variable's string value
conditions.expected_value: PL/pgSQL functions with CURSOR FOR declarations

evidence.quote_or_summary: Previously, the string value of such variables was set to match the variable name during cursor assignment; now it will be assigned during OPEN, and will not match the variable name. To restore the previous behavior, assign the desired portal name to the cursor variable before OPEN.
evidence.relevance: Describes the behavior change and workaround

ambiguities: Not clear how common it is for applications to depend on cursor variable string values matching variable names

suggested_actions: Search for PL/pgSQL functions that declare bound cursors (CURSOR FOR syntax)
Review code that accesses cursor variable string values or portal names
If the old behavior is needed, explicitly assign the desired portal name to the cursor variable before OPEN
Test all PL/pgSQL functions with cursors to verify correct behavior after upgrade

path_name: GENERATED expression restrictions tightened on inherited and partitioned tables
description: PostgreSQL 16 tightened restrictions on GENERATED columns in inherited and partitioned tables. Columns of parent/partitioned and child/partition tables must all have the same generation status (all GENERATED or all not), though the actual generation expressions can now differ. Existing schemas that violate this may fail to restore or cause errors.

conditions.statement: Target PostgreSQL version is 16 or later

evidence.quote_or_summary: Tighten GENERATED expression restrictions on inherited and partitioned tables
evidence.relevance: Documents the tightened restrictions in PostgreSQL 16

evidence.relevance: Specifies the new requirement for generation status consistency

ambiguities: Not clear what happens to existing schemas that violate this - whether pg_upgrade will fail or data will be rejected

suggested_actions: Query pg_attribute for tables with inheritance or partitioning that have GENERATED columns
Verify that parent and child tables have matching generation status (attgenerated) for corresponding columns
Adjust schema to ensure consistent generation status across inheritance hierarchies before upgrade

path_name: CREATEROLE privileges restricted, now requires ADMIN OPTION for many operations
description: PostgreSQL 16 significantly restricted the privileges of roles with CREATEROLE. Previously, CREATEROLE allowed modifying many aspects of any non-superuser role. Now, modifying roles (including adding members, changing CREATEDB, REPLICATION, BYPASSRLS properties) requires the role requesting the change to have ADMIN OPTION permission. Applications or administrative scripts that rely on CREATEROLE to manage other roles may fail with permission denied errors.

conditions.statement: Target PostgreSQL version is 16 or later

evidence.quote_or_summary: Restrict the privileges of CREATEROLE and its ability to modify other roles
evidence.relevance: Documents the privilege restriction in PostgreSQL 16

conditions.statement: Application or administrative scripts use roles with CREATEROLE privilege to modify other roles, add role members, or change role properties
conditions.expected_value: ALTER ROLE, GRANT role membership by CREATEROLE users

evidence.quote_or_summary: Previously roles with CREATEROLE privileges could change many aspects of any non-superuser role. Such changes, including adding members, now require the role requesting the change to have ADMIN OPTION permission. For example, they can now change the CREATEDB, REPLICATION, and BYPASSRLS properties only if they also have those permissions.
evidence.relevance: Describes the scope of the restriction and new requirements

suggested_actions: Audit roles with CREATEROLE privilege and what role management operations they perform
Review administrative scripts that use CREATEROLE roles to modify other roles or grant memberships
Grant ADMIN OPTION on managed roles to the CREATEROLE users that need to modify them
Test role management procedures in a non-production PostgreSQL 16 environment to identify permission issues

path_name: Role inheritance behavior changed to be set at GRANT time with new INHERIT clause
description: PostgreSQL 16 changed how role inheritance works. Previously, inheritance status was controlled only by the member role's inheritance attribute, affecting all memberships. Now, inheritance is controlled at GRANT time with the new WITH INHERIT clause, allowing different inheritance behavior for different role memberships. Existing role memberships will have their inheritance behavior migrated during upgrade, but scripts that rely on the old behavior may produce different results.

conditions.statement: Target PostgreSQL version is 16 or later

evidence.quote_or_summary: Role inheritance now controls the default inheritance status of member roles added during GRANT
evidence.relevance: Documents the fundamental change in role inheritance behavior

conditions.statement: Application or database design relies on role inheritance behavior, particularly changing a role's inheritance attribute to affect existing memberships
conditions.expected_value: GRANT role memberships with inheritance expectations

evidence.quote_or_summary: The role's default inheritance behavior can be overridden with the new GRANT ... WITH INHERIT clause. This allows inheritance of some roles and not others because the members' inheritance status is set at GRANT time. Previously the inheritance status of member roles was controlled only by the role's inheritance status, and changes to a role's inheritance status affected all previous and future member roles.
evidence.relevance: Explains the new GRANT-time inheritance control and how it differs from previous behavior

ambiguities: Migration behavior for existing role memberships is not fully specified in the provided chunks

suggested_actions: Review all GRANT role membership statements and role inheritance dependencies
Test role permission behavior after upgrade, particularly for roles that previously changed their inheritance attribute
Use the new WITH INHERIT clause explicitly in GRANT statements to ensure expected inheritance behavior
Query pg_auth_members to verify inheritance settings for role memberships after upgrade
